archival_memory.user_crush_description: She is in the same advanced algorithms class and was on the same project team. She has a great sense of humor, is witty, and keeps the mood light even in stressful situations. They share similar tastes in humor, which is refreshing.
archival_memory.complementary_strengths: You and your crush have complementary strengths. She excels in mathematics and discrete structures, while you have interests in software, system design, and data science. This complementarity helped you work well together on the project, and you appreciate her ability to explain complex concepts in a step-by-step manner.
archival_memory.friendship_at_college: Friendship is a huge topic for me because, in a lot of ways, my closest friends have become my second family at college. I've been here for four years, and I always say that as much as I love studying computer science, the people I've met along the way are what really keep me grounded and happy. Ironically, when I first arrived on campus, I thought that making friends might be more challenging—it was my first time living away from home, and I was nervous about whether I'd fit in. But over time, I ended up forming these really tight bonds that, honestly, have made all the stresses and workload of being a CS major feel way more manageable.
archival_memory.friendship_at_college_short: I've formed tight bonds with friends who have become my second family at college. They keep me grounded and happy, making the stresses of being a CS major manageable.
archival_memory.roommate_best_friend: I should start with my roommate and best friend from freshman year, Tony. We didn't know each other before that first semester, but we clicked right away over a conversation about a piece of software I was trying to prototype for an Intro to Programming class project. Tony's not even a CS major - he's in mechanical engineering - but we would bounce ideas off each other late into the night. We realized we had more in common than we initially thought. We both love working with our hands, albeit in different ways: I love to code and design logic, while he loves building things physically. We ended up collaborating on a few cross-disciplinary robotics projects since then, and we've grown closer because of those shared interests. Tony's someone I can always call when I'm overwhelmed with an assignment or if I just want to grab a pizza after a long day.

archival_memory.sailing_club_friends: I also have friends I met through the campus sailing club. It's amazing how many CS students I found there - we like to decompress by hitting the water. Sailing creates a fun mix of personalities, and we treat sailing strategy like a puzzle. The camaraderie on the boat is unique - we have to trust each other in high-stakes situations. We meet at odd hours to catch the best conditions, so we rely on each other for motivation. There's a deep mutual respect because we see each other's strengths and vulnerabilities. It's a great feeling to look across the sailboat and see a friend give you a thumbs-up after a tricky maneuver. One friend, Mariah, has become a close confidante. She encouraged me to apply for a challenging research position in data science, telling me to believe in my skills. That's the kind of unwavering support we have for each other.

archival_memory.cs_class_connections: I've made connections through my computer science classes, like study groups, group projects, and late-night coding sessions in the lab. There's a sense of solidarity from going through those tough times together. I remember this one time in my sophomore year, we were working on a systems programming course and had to build a mini operating system kernel from scratch. We were all struggling with memory management bugs, and it was just me and Carla left in the lab at 3 a.m. We bonded over pizza and ended up becoming close friends. Who would have thought that our struggles with pointers and memory leaks would lead to such a treasured friendship?

archival_memory.gym_friends: I also have friends from the gym. Working out has always been a way for me to unwind, and over time, I met a group of regulars who became a friendly circle. One of them, Dean, is a fellow CS major with a passion for machine learning and hardware acceleration. We started discussing our classes between sets, which led to sharing notes and eventually becoming gym buddies who exchange nutritional tips, workout routines, and more. We even game together now. He introduced me to a new co-op adventure game, and it's become a friendship built on mutual support, pushing each other to be better in various areas of life.

There's something special about gaming with a group in the same room - the laughs, inside jokes, and the excitement of a last-second victory. I made a great friend, Derek, through the club. He's super skilled in networking security and taught me some techniques that were useful in a cybersecurity research project. archival_memory.library_friendship: I also have a friend from the campus library. I spend a lot of time there studying, and over the years, I've met some regulars. One of them is Jackson, a law student who was reading case studies next to my stack of cryptography textbooks. We started chatting during water breaks, comparing our workloads. We discovered a shared interest in debating the ethical implications of new technologies. I'd talk to him for hours about algorithmic bias. archival_memory.everyday_life_friends: I've made friends in unexpected everyday situations, like in the dorm laundry room or while waiting in line for coffee. One day, I was super stressed with a research deadline and was waiting in a long line at the campus cafe. I was complaining under my breath about needing more time for my research code to run. The person behind me heard me and turned out to be going through her own mechanical engineering lab fiasco. We commiserated, shared a laugh, and ended up sitting together for coffee. We bonded over academic stress and exchanged contact info. Now, whenever we see each other on campus, we make a point to catch up. It's a positive, supportive relationship that started organically.
archival_memory.unifying_factor: What unifies all these friendships is mutual respect and the sense that we're navigating this crazy journey together. My experience as a computer science major has been the opposite of what people often think - we form deep connections, especially when the workload and pressure are high. We're in labs critiquing each other's code or on Slack until the crack of dawn, throwing out Hail Mary solutions to bugs. These challenges bond us. It's not always about competition; it's about how well we can collaborate and support each other.
archival_memory.graduation_and_goodbyes: As a fourth-year, graduation is looming, and it's bittersweet. I'm excited about the future - internships, job prospects, and maybe grad school. However, I'm also dreading the day when all these friends I've made scatter to different corners of the world. I keep reminding myself that some of these friendships are built to last. We've already talked about planning reunions, visiting each other if we end up in different cities, and staying connected online. It's weird thinking about how we'll be grown adults in different jobs, possibly different time zones, but hopefully still able to maintain the bond we forged here.
archival_memory.transcending_distance: I believe real friendship is about having a strong sense of trust, loyalty, and empathy that can transcend distance. I see that in Tony, who's interning across the country this semester, yet we still FaceTime regularly. I see the same dedication in others, like Carla, who's applying to master's programs abroad. We promised that if either of us ends up in Europe, the other has to come visit. It's amazing how these bonds can endure despite physical distance.
archival_memory.gratitude_for_friends: I'm extremely grateful for the friendships I've made through sailing, the gym, gaming, research, and random campus encounters. They're an integral part of my college experience, reminding me that there's more to this journey than just achievements on my resume. If I log off Zoom or finish a lab feeling like I can call these people my friends, that's what success really looks like to me. I know that no matter where I end up in my career, I'll carry a piece of each of these friends with me. Friends aren't just a chapter in your life story; they can be co-authors, helping you write the best parts.
